newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore government securities end narrowly mixed.
newsitem.headline: Singapore government securities end narrowly mixed.

text.p: Singapore government securities ended narrowly mixed in moderate trade on retail and interbank interest, dealers said on Tuesday.

"The interbank rate rose slightly today but there was little impact on the market. Treasury bill yields were steady to slightly higher but bond prices were slightly lower. Volume was moderate," a local dealer said.
In treasury bills, three-months closed at a yield of 2.18/2.13 percent compared with Monday's yield of 2.13/2.08 percent. One-year was unchanged from Monday's yield of 2.30/2.25 percent.
Among bonds, July 1998 ended at S$98.00/98.05 against Monday's close of S$98.05/98.10, September 2001 at S$96.95/97.00 versus S$97.05/97.10 and June 2003 at S$94.95/95.00 from S$95.05/95.10.
The overnight interbank offered rate rose to 2-3/4 2-5/8 percent against Monday's 2-5/8 2-1/2 percent.
